Maya (PM): FYI customer X wants concrete 'optimize toolkit' recommendations for batching/caching/quant by next week. can we outline acceptance criteria so Solutions can sign off?
Jamie (Eng): quick q — do they expect per-endpoint recs or general guidance?
Tia (Solutions): per-endpoint would be ideal (chat vs completion vs embeddings). they sent a few latency targets and cost ceilings.
Maya (PM): they gave: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 200ms, cost reduction goal 20% vs current. also need rollback plan.
Omar (Eng-ML): ok — that's tight for chat. I'd propose: 1) benchmarked baseline; 2) quant profile A/B with quality guardrails; 3) adaptive batching policy with per-model max batch size and timeout; 4) prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.
Alex (Research): important: quantization can give +3-6x perf but some prompts degrade. we should require eval-triggered alerts on quality drift tied to our regression suite.
Jamie (Eng): propose launch gates: - Canary at 5% for 24h, then 25% for 48h; metrics: token/sec, p95 latency, error rate, and quality-concordance (eval set). fail if quality-concordance drops >2% absolute.
Tia (Solutions): customers will want explicit config examples. can we produce a sample policy?
Jamie (Eng): sure — rough example: ```
optimize_policy:
  model: redwood-3b
  batching:
    max_batch: 32
    latency_budget_ms: 100
  caching:
    kv_prefix_ttl: 300s
  quantization:
    profile: int8_dynamic
    fallback_on_quality_loss: true
  eval_alerts:
    enabled: true
    threshold_abs_drop: 0.02
```
Maya (PM): love it. also add cost SLO: unit-token-cost <= 0.8x baseline or include regression explanation. customer may accept tradeoffs if we document expected fail modes.
Omar (Eng-ML): note: fallback_on_quality_loss needs a realtime signal — we'll wire eval-triggered alerts + auto-fallback to float16 variant. that requires KV cache invalidation when rolling back.
Alex (Research): for eval-triggered alerts let's pin the initial eval set to 200 prompts across high-sensitivity flows. run daily and on canary snapshots.
Tia (Solutions): acceptance checklist for handoff to field: docs + config example + runbook (how to abort, how to increase canary), cost analysis, and a template customer-facing email. can we commit to that for next Tue?
Jamie (Eng): dev time estimate: 3 dev-days for policy scaffolding + 2 days for alert plumbing + 1 day for docs. QA/canary monitoring will be ongoing.
Maya (PM): ok — I'll draft acceptance criteria doc and ping legal for customer comms. @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary run template?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary template created: /deploys/canary-optimize-1741234567. visibility: product, eng, solutions. :robot_face:
Maya (PM): thanks. next steps: Jamie/Omar produce config + plumbing PR, Alex prepare eval set, Tia draft customer handoff. syncing Fri EOD to review artifacts. :thumbsup:
